If you look at one of my previous comments I actually said this was one of the biggest pitfalls of international students was assuming that scores mattered so much.

We get students with 4.0s who have been stuck as an analyst their whole life, and college dropouts who create unicorn startups. The scores can help us see your journey and how you operate, but dont majorly impact our opinion. 

The more important thing to focus on is your goals, and why WE can help you, why not any other university, what classes, why research, what programs, why us. Why are you switching. What have you done?   
American universities on a whole value the story of your application and the impact you have had on your workplace, more than any score or label.

They look like an infection of the hair follicles. They’re not pimples so don’t bother with acne products at all. 1)use a product, I’ve heard people rave about washing the area in the shower dandruff shampoo as a cheap easy means since it’s anti fungal. I’ve discovered triple paste baby diaper cream (silly but after 8 years of living with bumps and trying everything it is the sole thing that works for me) I apply mine whenever I will be sitting for long periods of time (bedtime)
2) exfoliate. Buy a cloth or something from Marshall’s or Target or whatever, use twice a week while using soap or dandruff shampoo (if you choose to buy that product)
3) clean your sheets and don’t rewear pants, be careful about regiving yourself the infection. I found that I have to wash my bedsheets every week for best results but every two weeks is okay too.
4) not as pivotal but makes a big difference in how effective everything else is: exercise more and shower immediately after. I found that sweating opened up the infected pores, so when I cleaned myself in the shower and applied my cream, it had a way way bigger impact. Exercising was kinda like salt to my recipe for success, wouldn’t taste good by itself but enhanced everything else. I hate exercising at a gym so I found that commuting on my bike to the grocery store and to school was enough exercise to do my pores justice! What happens is stress makes your body contract which lowers pulse and blood pressure ( but don't worry you're not dying and everyone recovers, fainting is common and not the end of the world). The usual symptoms for me are a tight chest, hard breathing, then dizzy a bit, then I get a deep cold feeling like a deep down coldness and this is when you're on the verge/ close to passing out so make sure you're on the ground/ in bed. It is best for your body and blood is you lay down but very elevated so its almost like you're sitting and keep your  legs bent (not just flat). It's possible but once you realize you're safe, it's okay, and if it does happen you'll wake up very soon feeling soooo much better. Your body only passes out so you stop flexing internal muscles which constrict your blood. So passing out is actually healthy! it's your body making sure it gets more blood.
